facts.text: Brock University is the city's largest employer with 5,965 employees, followed by the Niagara Health System and the District School Board of Niagara.
Niagara Health provides acute care hospital services to the 450,000 residents of the Niagara region with more than 7,300 employees, physicians, volunteers and patient partners.
General Motors Canada has completed a $28-million cogeneration investment at its St. Catharines Propulsion plant, lowering emissions and future energy costs.
facts.publisher: InvestInSTC (City of St. Catharines Economic Development)

facts.text: Health care assets are coming together in St. Catharines through Niagara Health, Brock's Cairns Family Health and Biosciences Research Complex and McMaster's satellite medical campus.

overview: St. Catharines counted 136,803 residents in the 2021 Census, up 2.8% from 133,113 in 2016. The median age is 44.8, several years older than most Ontario cities, and the median household income in 2020 was $72,500, so this is a mature market where value and trust matter more than novelty.

The city's 58,903 occupied dwellings sit on 96.2 square kilometres, and the biggest employers are Brock University, Niagara Health and the school board. Local businesses compete for a stable, slow-growing customer base.
